Overview

GCG is seeking a Product Line Manager to lead the commercial and operational performance of our OEM cable assembly business within our Custom Engineered Solutions (CES) division!

This is a highly analytical role supporting more than $60 million in OEM business across four manufacturing and operating facilities.

Reporting to our Vice President of Assembly, you will help leadership understand how the business is performing across product lines, customers, facilities, and part numbers. You will analyze margins, sales trends, finished-goods inventory, customer forecasts, commodity costs, pricing, backlog, and other performance indicators, then turn that information into clear recommendations for our Sales, Operations, Supply Chain, and Finance leaders.

You will also improve forecasting and analytical models, validate existing business-intelligence reporting, build CES-specific dashboards where reporting gaps exist, and help coordinate cross-functional initiatives involving pricing, inventory, cost reduction, new-part introductions, and process improvement.

This is a remote position requiring the employee to work from the Eastern or Central Time Zone. The role may require approximately quarterly travel, primarily to GCG facilities.

  • Develop actionable recommendations that improve profitability, pricing strategy, inventory performance, and customer service.

  • Professional experience within manufacturing or industrial distribution

  • Demonstrated experience analyzing sales, inventory, pricing, forecasting, margin, or other operational and commercial data

  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including experience creating and maintaining multi-sheet workbooks, pivot tables, lookups, dashboards, and data-validation tools

  • Experience extracting, reconciling, validating, and interpreting information from ERP, business-intelligence, or related business systems

  • Strong organizational and project-coordination skills, including the ability to manage multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholder needs

  • Clear written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present analysis and recommendations to leadership

  • Ability to influence work, coordinate priorities, and provide functional direction without formal reporting authority

  • Ability to work remotely from the Eastern or Central Time Zone and align working hours with applicable teams and stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications

GCG’s Custom Engineered Solutions division supports original equipment manufacturers and other customers with customized wire, cable, connectivity, and assembly solutions designed around their technical, operational, and supply-chain requirements.

At GCG, our mission is to power, connect, and automate our world. With the responsive DNA of a startup and the size of a global leader, we offer top brands and extensive value-added services that make us an invaluable partner to our customers in multiple industry verticals across the globe.

jobs.description:
The ideal candidate combines the commercial instincts of a salesperson with the analytical and product skills of a well-trained merchant/buyer.

About Shinesty

At Shinesty, our mission is to force the world to take itself less seriously. We make people laugh first and sell second. Our mothers don’t always approve of what we do, but the millions of people we’ve entertained over the years do. We're best known for Ball Hammock® pouch underwear, bold prints, and an irreverent brand voice, with an assortment spanning underwear, socks, swim, loungewear, apparel, and accessories. Wholesale is one of our largest growth opportunities, and we're building the team to turn strong initial retailer performance into larger assortments, more departments, and chainwide expansion.

The Role

You will own, grow, and strengthen Shinesty's most important retail partnerships. This is not a passive account-management role: you're accountable for understanding each retailer's business, improving sell-through, increasing reorders, expanding assortments, and earning additional doors.

You'll work on a two person team with our Key Account Executive, who is primarily responsible for opening new accounts and relationships.

Our new-business sales lead owns: prospecting and opening new retail accounts, securing meetings with new buyers, leading initial sell-in presentations, negotiating the first commercial commitment, and cross selling new products where categories are bought by different functions within one organization.

You own: account strategy and buyer communication, reorders and sell-through performance, marketing activations, merchandising, door expansion, forecasting and execution, and long-term revenue growth.

Both of you will participate in important pitches and expansion opportunities. The retailer should experience one coordinated Shinesty team with clear internal ownership and no dropped handoffs. Your success will be measured as a team.

Key-account growth

  • Own the day-to-day and strategic relationships with assigned wholesale accounts once they are handed over.
  • Build annual and seasonal account plans covering revenue, assortment, doors, departments, and promotions.
  • Grow revenue through reorders, expanded assortments, new categories, and increased door penetration.
  • Identify underperforming stores, products, and programs, and build clear plans to fix them.
  • Turn strong sell-through into persuasive expansion recommendations for buyers and senior merchants.
  • Ensure we get pre-books from key accounts in advance of production.

Buyer relationships

  • Build trusted relationships with buyers, merchants, planners, and allocators at each account.
  • Develop a detailed understanding of each retailer's customer, assortment strategy, calendar, and internal decision-making.
  • Lead recurring business reviews, line reviews, and sell-through conversations on a consistent cadence.
  • Present performance and opportunities in a way that helps buyers advocate for Shinesty internally.

Assortment & merchandising strategy

  • Use account-, SKU-, and door-level data to recommend the right products, quantities, pricing, and promotions.
  • Partner with design, product, and merchandising to build retailer-specific assortments and represent wholesale in internal planning.
  • Analyze sales, margin, inventory, turns, weeks of supply, and units per door per week.
  • Identify assortment gaps that could unlock meaningful wholesale growth.

Replenishment & forecasting

  • Monitor sell-through, inventory levels, and order patterns across accounts to spot replenishment needs before the retailer does.
  • Build and maintain replenishment forecasts and reorder recommendations with planning and supply chain.
  • Track fill rates, in-stocks, and lead times; flag risks to on-time, in-full delivery.
  • Maintain accurate account forecasts by retailer, category, and season, and keep account plans, pipelines, and next actions current in our CRM.

Requirements

Particularly Relevant Backgrounds

We're especially interested in candidates who trained as a Buyer, Merchant, or Merchandise Manager in a respected retail development program and have since moved — or want to move — to the brand side. Category experience in men's apparel, underwear, socks, accessories, outdoor, gifting, or seasonal is a plus, as is familiarity with retailers like Tractor Supply, Scheels, Boot Barn, Murdoch's, Dick’s, Bass Pro, or other like retailers.

What We're Looking For

  • 5–10 years in retail merchandising, buying, or wholesale account management.
  • Comfort selling to retail buyers and asking for what you want
  • Experience owning a category, a major retailer relationship, or a meaningful portion of a retail business.
  • Strong retail math: sales, margin, inventory, turns, weeks of supply, markdowns, units per door per week.
  • Proven ability to turn analysis into a clear commercial recommendation and present it to buyers or senior retail stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication, relationship-building, and negotiation skills; able to influence without formal authority.
  • High ownership, urgency, and follow-through; comfortable in an entrepreneurial company without big-company support structure.
  • Willingness to travel for retailer meetings, line reviews, store visits, and trade shows.

You May Not Be the Right Fit If

  • You view account management primarily as responding to retailer requests.
  • You're uncomfortable selling - asking a buyer for more doors, more assortment, or a larger commitment.
  • You rely on relationships without supporting recommendations with data or you're highly analytical but don't enjoy selling and presenting.
  • You wait for opportunities to be assigned rather than actively identifying them.
  • You're uncomfortable representing a bold, irreverent consumer brand.

What Success Looks Like in 12 Months

  • Account plans and a consistent business-review cadence in place for every assigned strategic retailer.
  • Net revenue retention above 120% on your assigned account base — existing accounts grow, they don't leak.
  • Reactivated or rebuilt the majority of assigned accounts that lapsed or declined in the prior year.
  • Measurably improved reorder rates, assortment depth, and units per door per week across priority accounts.
  • At least one new department or category launched within multiple existing retail partners.
  • Forecast accuracy and wholesale demand visibility materially improved for planning and operations.
  • > 60% of prebooks placed before the season deadline.

Benefits

  • Work from home (please note travel is expected, extensively at some points)
  • 2027 On Target Earnings: $100k-$140k (please note this is a mix of base and sales-based bonus/commission)
  • Laptop + whatever other equipment you need
  • Access to any AI platform that will make you better at your job
  • Medical, dental, vision insurance
  • Dog-friendly office
  • Flexible PTO, no need to accrue time take as much as you’d like
  • Flexible working hours, get your work done and generate results
  • Discounted and free products
  • Work every day with an incredibly smart, fun, and creative team

About PatientIQ

PatientIQ is a fast-growing health tech company on a mission to improve patient outcomes. We partner with healthcare providers, medical device companies, and researchers to collect, analyze, and act on patient-reported outcomes data at scale — powering smarter clinical decisions and accelerating the future of value-based care.

Headquartered in Chicago and backed by top-tier venture capital and major health system investors, PatientIQ is building the largest platform for healthcare providers, industry partners, and researchers to collaborate on what matters most: helping patients get better.

The opportunity

PatientIQ is expanding into cardiovascular medicine, and we are hiring a dedicated Account Executive to accelerate our growth in this high-priority specialty. PatientIQ already has deep relationships with leading health systems across the country — this role is about activating those relationships in cardiology service lines, opening new doors within and adjacent to our existing network, and owning the full commercial cycle to build meaningful market share in cardiovascular care.

This is not an account management role or a territory management role. This is a commercial role focused on market development: establishing PatientIQ as the go-to platform for cardiovascular programs — across health system CV service lines, independent cardiovascular practices, and the society ecosystem (ACC, AHA, STS) — by leveraging your network and ours to drive pipeline, close business, and shape the commercial playbook for cardiology at scale.

The Cardiovascular Specialty AE will own the full new logo sales cycle — from prospect identification through contract execution — with direct support from the PatientIQ Customer Success team for post-sale onboarding and expansion. You will also partner closely with PatientIQ’s Outcomes Research & Registries team, which co-owns the STS registry relationship and positions PatientIQ as the EHR-integrated data capture and registry submission platform for cardiovascular programs. This role sits within the Provider Sales organization, reporting to the VP of Sales.

What you'll do

NEW LOGO ACQUISITION

  • Territory ownership: Own and build the cardiovascular new logo pipeline across cardiovascular practices, NSPs with cardiology service lines, and health systems with dedicated cardiovascular programs.
  • Full-cycle sales: Prospect, qualify, demo, negotiate, and close.
  • Pipeline accountability: Maintain 3× pipeline coverage against your quarterly target. Accurate, weekly HubSpot forecast hygiene is a non-negotiable.

MARKET DEVELOPMENT & SOCIETY RELATIONSHIPS

  • ACC, AHA & STS alignment: Leverage existing society relationships and partner with PatientIQ's Outcomes Research & Registries team to co-develop registry-linked commercial propositions and expand STS co-ownership to new program sites.
  • CMS cardiac episode model positioning: Position PatientIQ as the data infrastructure layer enabling cardiovascular programs to participate in CMS Accountable Care for Stroke and cardiac episode payment models — a near-term, high-urgency buyer trigger.
  • Conference presence: Represent PatientIQ at ACC, AHA, SCAI, and STS annual meetings. Build relationships at the clinical and administrative decision-maker level before active sales cycles begin.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL EXECUTION

  • Outcomes Research coordination: Work closely with the Outcomes Research & Registries team on research-adjacent sales opportunities, registry positioning, and sponsored research leads from cardiovascular device manufacturers.
  • CSM partnership: Partner with the CSM team (Enterprise and Specialty tracks) for post-sale onboarding, expansion identification, and strategic account development. You are responsible for new logo velocity; the CSM team carries retention and expansion.
  • Product feedback loop: Serve as the voice of the cardiovascular buyer to Product and Clinical teams — surfacing workflow gaps, data capture requirements, and registry integration needs unique to cardiovascular programs.

What success looks like

We believe clarity drives performance. Here's what the first 90 days look like in this role:

30 days - Pipeline built — 10+ qualified cardiovascular opportunities identified and active in HubSpot. Society relationship map and existing network contacts documented; STS registry positioning briefed with team

60 days - First demo cycle active; 2+ opportunities at proposal stage. Coordinated with Outcomes Research & Registries on registry co-positioning; ACC conference strategy in place

90 days - First signed agreement — minimum $80K ACV. Pipeline at 3× quarterly target; CMS cardiac episode model positioning in active use with prospects

Requirements

What you bring

Required

  • Cardiovascular network: You have existing relationships with cardiovascular program directors, cardiology practice administrators, quality officers, or cardiovascular service line leaders at health systems or NSPs.
  • Clinical technology sales: 5+ years of B2B sales experience in health IT, digital health, or clinical technology with a consistent track record of closing six-figure deals.
  • Full-cycle ownership: Demonstrated experience owning the full sales cycle from cold outreach through contract signature — including navigating procurement, legal, and multi-stakeholder sign-off.
  • Society and registry fluency: Working knowledge of the ACC, AHA, and/or STS registry ecosystem; familiarity with CMS cardiac episode payment model requirements.
  • Outcomes data literacy: Able to credibly discuss patient-reported outcomes, registry submission workflows, EHR integration requirements, and clinical quality measurement with physician and quality leader audiences.
  • CRM discipline: HubSpot (preferred) or Salesforce proficiency — accurate pipeline entry, opportunity stage management, and weekly forecast hygiene.

Nice to have

  • CMS quality payment programs: Experience selling into cardiovascular programs participating in TAVR, CABG, or Stroke episode payment models.
  • Medical device commercial background: Experience selling to or alongside cardiovascular device manufacturers (Medtronic, Boston Scientific, Abbott) — familiarity with their data requirements and post-market surveillance workflows.

Benefits

Why PatientIQ

  • Mission-driven work. We're solving a hard problem that matters — improving patient outcomes through better data. Every person here is working on something real.
  • True idea meritocracy. Great ideas win, regardless of title. We encourage every team member to challenge the status quo.
  • World-class team. You'll work alongside people who are at the top of their fields in health tech, enterprise software, and clinical science.
  • Fast-growing. We're building the largest platform for healthcare providers and industry to collaborate — and we're just getting started.
  • Great benefits. Top-notch health, dental, and vision. 401(k). Flexible PTO — we trust you to take the time you need. Professional development stipends.
  • Real ownership. This is not a role where you maintain someone else's playbook. You'll build, shape strategy, and see your impact directly.

jobs.excerpt: Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults.
jobs.description:
Prosper Health is on a mission to make life happier and healthier for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

Despite autism diagnoses increasing more than 5x in the past 25 years, autistic adults have been systematically overlooked. This has led to extremely poor outcomes, including high rates of co-occurring mental health conditions and a lower life expectancy. Prosper is here to change that.

We deliver specialized mental health services for autistic adults, covered by insurance. We've helped tens of thousands of people receive an autism diagnosis for the first time, work with neurodivergent-affirming therapists, and find belonging through community. Our outcomes meaningfully outperform traditional care for autistic adults, with substantially greater improvements in mood, anxiety, and quality of life.

Prosper is growing 3x year over year and are at mid-double-digit millions in run-rate revenue, with thousands of active clients and 400+ clinicians. We're a high-ownership, mission-driven team, building something that has never existed for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

The Opportunity

We're hiring Licensed Mental Health Therapists (LCSW, LPC, LMHC) to provide therapy for autistic and neurodivergent adults via telehealth. You'll join a team dedicated to creating affirming, accessible mental health services for the neurodivergent community.

Our clinicians come from diverse backgrounds and career stages - whether you're passionate about neurodiversity advocacy, seeking flexibility and better work-life balance, or looking to add specialized experience to your existing practice, we offer roles to match your professional goals.

Why Therapists Choose Prosper:

  • Focus on what matters most: Provide exceptional client care while we manage administrative tasks, insurance billing, and client acquisition
  • Enjoy scheduling flexibility: Design your work schedule to accommodate personal needs and maintain optimal work-life balance
  • Scale your practice quickly: Build your caseload with steady client referrals during your first few weeks, with most clinicians reaching their ideal caseload within 4-6 weeks
  • No-show and late cancellation reimbursement: Receive 50% reimbursement for late cancellations and no-shows
  • Grow professionally: Access regular peer consultation, specialized training, and monthly case conferences
  • Neurodiversity-affirming environment: Work alongside clinicians who share your commitment to neurodiversity-affirming approaches
  • Connect with a supportive clinical community: Join weekly drop-ins and engage in a tight-knit clinical community that prevent isolation

We offer two distinct position types to accommodate different career needs and scheduling preferences

Scheduling Availability

  • Set your own schedule, 7 days a week, between 7am and 10pm
  • No required evening, weekend or on-call hours
  • Build your schedule around your life, not the other way around

Full time (Benefits-Eligible)

  • Hours: Provide 25+ hours of weekly availability to build a caseload of 25+ clients
  • Ideal for: Those who seek steady, predictable income that grows with your client base
  • Compensation: Competitive hourly rate paid per session
  • Benefits: Comprehensive benefits package including Medical/Dental/Vision coverage, 401(k) retirement plan and PTO.

Part-Time Position

  • Hours: Provide 15+ hours of weekly availability to build a caseload of 15+ clients
  • Ideal For: Practitioners with existing commitments who want to diversify their practice or add specialized neurodiversity experience to your clinical portfolio
  • Compensation: Competitive hourly rate paid per session

Who We're Looking For:

Qualifications:

  • Licensed independent mental health professional (LCSW, LPC, LMHC)
  • Strong clinical skills in evidence-based modalities such as CBT, DBT or ACT
  • Interest in working with autistic or neurodivergent adults
  • Comfort with technology and virtual care platforms (Zoom, EHR, Slack)
  • Excellent communication skills and commitment to client-centered care
  • Telehealth experience preferred but not required

You'll Thrive Here If:

  • You identify with our mission to support the neurodivergent community
  • You're seeking better work-life balance without sacrificing meaningful clinical work
  • You're transitioning from a demanding in-person setting and want more flexibility
  • You want to maintain multiple practice settings and add specialized experience
  • You're passionate about providing affirming care to traditionally underserved populations

Compensation:

Our transparent model means your income grows with your client relationships. Unlike traditional salary models, our fee-for-service approach rewards you directly for the sessions you provide. The more sessions you complete, the more your practice thrives – with the security of guaranteed income during no-shows and cancellations. We pay between $X - $X per session.

Join Our Team

Ready to transform lives while advancing your career? Apply today to join Prosper Health's team of dedicated professionals making a real difference for autistic and neurodivergent adults.

Prosper Health is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse and inclusive team. We encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, including those who identify as neurodivergent, LGBTQ+, or BIPOC.

Competitive W2 rate paid per session. 50% reimbursement for late cancellations/no shows. Paid every 2 weeks for the sessions you provide, no waiting for payment or reimbursement. Benefit Eligible roles available that include Medical/Dental/Vision/401k/PTO

W2 Per Session Rate
$55—$60 USD

More about Prosper Health

  • Our culture is a unique mix of thoughtfulness, kindess, and high-performance. We set ambitious goals and hold ourselves accountable to achieving them.
  • We always ensure that we integrate perspectives from experts in our space, including clinicians and autistic self-advocates.
  • Our team members come from places such as Bain, McKinsey, BCG, FirstHand Health, Rula, SeatGeek, Benchling, and schools like Harvard, MIT, Stanford, Yale, Penn, Dartmouth, Northwestern, Vanderbilt, and more.
  • Here are a few of our favorite operating principles:
    • Clients first - Our job is to solve real problems for our clients. Choose what makes life better for the client, even if it’s harder for us. Never lose sight of the person on the other side.
    • Find a Way - We use ingenuity, scrappiness, and determination to bend the world to accomplish our goals. We’re resourceful and do more with less.
    • Raise the Bar - We grow deliberately, by asking how things can improve and by giving and seeking feedback. We insist on the highest standards and keep pushing them higher.
    • Be a Good Person - Be kind, be honest, and make it fun to work here. Tell the truth even when it’s uncomfortable. Treat people with respect and go out of your way to do nice things for your teammates.

jobs.description:
At Veracyte, we offer exciting career opportunities for those interested in joining a pioneering team that is committed to transforming cancer care for patients across the globe.   • We Are Stronger Together: We engage with empathy, align around what's best for Veracyte, and celebrate as one team.
  • We Care Deeply: We show up with integrity, kindness, and respect for one another.

The Position:

We are seeking an experienced Senior Clinical Reimbursement Specialist to serve as a clinical subject matter expert on our Clinical Reimbursement Operations team. In this role, you will independently manage complex pre- and post-service appeals, mentor junior team members, and drive process improvements that measurably improve overturn rates and revenue capture across the revenue cycle.

You will apply advanced clinical judgment and deep payer policy expertise to handle the team's most complex, high-dollar, and precedent-setting cases - including Level 2 appeals, external reviews, and payer escalations. Beyond individual casework, you will contribute to workflow design, SOP development, and cross-functional initiatives that strengthen the team's overall performance.

Success in this role requires advanced knowledge of reimbursement systems (including payer utilization management and claims adjudication), fluency in payer medical policies, sound and independent clinical judgment on complex cases, and the ability to influence outcomes through both direct case ownership and informal leadership.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Independently manage complex pre- and post-service appeals across Level 1, Level 2, and external review pathways, including the review, development, and submission of clinically robust appeal documentation.
  • Serve as a clinical subject matter expert on payer medical policies, translating complex policy criteria into patient-specific clinical justification and guiding appeal strategy for high-dollar, ambiguous, or precedent-setting cases.
  • Own end-to-end resolution of assigned cases, including follow-up, coordination with ordering providers, and appropriate escalation to leadership when warranted.
  • Partner with ordering physicians and practice staff to coordinate peer-to-peer reviews, gather supplemental clinical documentation, secure Authorized Representative forms and signatures, and support collaborative initiatives that strengthen appeal outcomes.
  • Mentor and provide informal guidance to Clinical Reimbursement Specialists, including case review, appeal letter quality feedback, and coaching on payer policy interpretation.
  • Lead analysis of denial patterns and appeal outcomes to identify root causes, and drive upstream feedback to reduce future denials.
  • Contribute directly to the development and refinement of appeal letter templates, clinical evidence packets, payer reference guides, and other scalable operational tools.
  • Monitor payer behavior and policy changes across all lines of business; flag material changes and partner with leadership on remediations, coverage reviews, and payer escalations.
  • Support the maintenance and continuous improvement of SOPs, ensuring workflows remain consistent, compliant, and scalable as the team grows.
  • Serve as point of contact for complex patient- or provider-facing inquiries, ensuring accurate, empathetic, and compliant communication.
  • Support digital transformation initiatives, including automation and AI/agentic workflow pilots that improve appeal readiness scoring and clinical documentation review.
  • Represent the Clinical Reimbursement team in cross-functional initiatives and special projects that support evolving reimbursement and operational priorities.

Who You Are:

Qualifications

Required

  • Active clinical licensure (e.g., RN, NP).
  • Associate or Bachelor's degree in nursing.
  • 3–5 years of experience in healthcare reimbursement, revenue cycle operations, or payer-facing roles.
  • 2+ years of experience in prior authorization, denial management, or appeals -including pre-service and post-service workflows.
  • Advanced understanding of payer medical policies, prior authorization, claims adjudication, denials, and appeals - including Level 1, Level 2, and external review processes.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex, ambiguous, or high-dollar cases without routine escalation.
  • Proven ability to translate complex payer medical policy criteria into patient-specific clinical justification.
  • Strong critical thinking and analytical skills, including the ability to interpret incomplete denial information and drive appropriate next steps without direction.
  • Experience contributing to the development of SOPs, appeal letter templates, workflow tools, or other operational assets within a reimbursement environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to mentor or provide informal leadership to peers, including case review, coaching, or SME support.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional discussions and convey clinical/reimbursement concepts to both clinical and non-clinical stakeholders.
  • Demonstrates ownership of cases through resolution, including follow-up, coordination, and appropriate escalation.
  • Comfortable working in an evolving environment with shifting priorities, ambiguity, and the need to build systems where none exist.

Preferred

  • Prior experience in oncology diagnostics, laboratory services, or complex/specialty reimbursement environments.
  • Experience leading or contributing to process improvement, workflow redesign, or operational scaling initiatives within the revenue cycle.
  • Familiarity with digital transformation initiatives in healthcare operations (automation, AI/agentic workflows, workflow tools, system integration).
  • Relevant certification (CPC, CRCR, CHFP, Lean/Six Sigma) or Master's degree (MSN, MHA, MBA).

The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to years of experience, skillset, geographic location, industry, education, etc. Base pay is one part of the Total Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and restricted stock units.

Pay range
$86,098—$107,850 USD

What We Can Offer You

Veracyte is a growing company that offers significant career opportunities if you are curious, driven, patient-oriented and aspire to help us build a great company. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, and are committed to fostering an inclusive workforce, where diverse backgrounds are represented, engaged, and empowered to drive innovative ideas and decisions. We are thrilled to be recognized as a 2024 Certified™ Great Place to Work® in both the US and Israel - a testament to our dynamic, inclusive, and inspiring workplace where passion meets purpose.

Veracyte (Nasdaq: VCYT) is a global diagnostics company whose vision is to transform cancer care for patients all over the world. We empower clinicians with the high-value insights they need to guide and assure patients at pivotal moments in the race to diagnose and treat cancer. Our Veracyte Diagnostics Platform delivers high-performing cancer tests that are fueled by broad genomic and clinical data, deep bioinformatic and AI capabilities, and a powerful evidence-generation engine, which ultimately drives durable reimbursement and guideline inclusion for our tests, along with new insights to support continued innovation and pipeline development. Pelago is the leading specialty substance use care provider, built on the belief that effective treatment means matching care intensity to what each member actually needs rather than defaulting to the most expensive intervention. Our programs guide members through every stage of the substance use spectrum, from unhealthy habits to active use disorders, delivering personalized treatment for tobacco, alcohol, opioid, cannabis, and stimulant use based on individual health, habits, genetics, and goals.

With Sona, our voice-first AI Mental Health Specialist, Pelago now applies that same clinically-driven model to mental health, pairing deep clinical expertise with technology to expand access without compromising care quality. We believe technology should make clinical care more precise and more human, not replace the judgment behind it.

Pelago has scaled to helping hundreds of employers and health plans and has already helped more than 750,000 members better manage their substance use. If you're passionate about AI and making an impact on the health of others, join us and make it happen!

Overview of the Role


We are seeking a Care Specialist to join our digital clinic and help members achieve healthier, more fulfilling lives. As the first point of contact, the Care Specialist plays a vital role in creating a welcoming onboarding experience and helping members successfully begin their care journey at Pelago. This role is primarily focused on conducting intake assessments, welcome calls, and initial clinical screenings, educating members on Pelago's care model, and connecting them with the appropriate ongoing care team.

Approximately 70% of this role is dedicated to member onboarding activities, including intakes, welcome calls, and care coordination. The remaining 30% focuses on maintaining a small ongoing caseload and providing flexible clinical support through temporary member coverage, pilot initiatives, and other operational needs. The ideal candidate is clinically strong, adaptable, enjoys variety, and is passionate about improving access to high-quality substance use care.
This is a direct-service, remote clinical role based anywhere in the USA.

In this role you will…
  • Serve as the first clinical point of contact for members entering Pelago, creating a welcoming, supportive onboarding experience.
  • Conduct initial screenings and intake assessments to evaluate behavioral health history, substance use, symptoms, and member goals.
  • Understand all Pelago care pathways, effectively communicate treatment options to members, and guide them toward the most appropriate level of care.
  • Facilitate warm transitions by connecting members with their assigned counselor or coach and sharing relevant clinical information to support continuity of care.
  • Conduct welcome calls and other early member touchpoints to build rapport, answer questions, increase engagement, and ensure a smooth transition into ongoing care.
  • Maintain a small ongoing caseload by providing individual counseling, monitoring progress toward behavior change goals, and supporting members as needed.
  • Provide temporary member coverage during clinician leave, staffing transitions, or other operational needs.
  • Support special projects, pilot programs, and new clinical workflows as needed.
  • Document member interactions thoroughly and contribute to ongoing quality improvement efforts.
  • Utilize evidence-based approaches including CBT, Motivational Interviewing (MI), mindfulness-based interventions, harm reduction techniques, and relapse prevention.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (including Product, Clinical, and Operations) to optimize the member experience and inform service improvements.
  • Maintain active licensure(s)/certification(s) in good standing and ensure compliance with all applicable regulations.

The background we are looking for...

  • 3+ years of clinical experience working with individuals with substance use disorders, with demonstrated expertise in CBT, MI, and relapse prevention.
  • Hold an active and unrestricted state credential (license/certification), issued via a state credentialing board. Multi-state licensure is preferred.

  • Experience providing SBIRT care for people with SUDs.
  • Excellent attention to detail and strong documentation skills.
  • Experience in program development and quality assurance in clinical settings.
  • Strong communication and organizational skills, with a track record of managing competing priorities.

Senior Web Content Strategist / Content Migration Lead

Contract | Remote, Canada | Potential travel within Canada

About the opportunity

Aequilibrium is assembling a senior Canadian team for a potential large-scale digital experience modernization initiative involving multiple public-facing websites and a substantial existing content estate. We are looking for a Senior Web Content Strategist / Content Migration Lead to help transform a large volume of existing content into a simpler, more useful and sustainable digital experience.

This isn't primarily a copywriting role. We're looking for someone who can develop the content strategy, lead a large-scale content audit, and guide content through a CMS migration. The hourly rate for this role is b/w $75/h-$95/h

What you'll do

  • Lead the content strategy for a multi-site, multi-brand digital ecosystem.
  • Develop and execute a structured content inventory and audit.
  • Establish criteria for what content should be retained, consolidated, rewritten, archived or retired.
  • Work with the Information Architect to improve content hierarchy, taxonomy, metadata and findability.
  • Define content models and support component-based content design.
  • Establish standards for plain language, readability, consistency and accessibility.
  • Help develop content governance, ownership and publishing workflows.
  • Work with business analysts and technical teams to plan and execute large-scale CMS content migration.
  • Help identify opportunities for automated versus manual migration.
  • Support URL mapping, redirects and SEO preservation.
  • Develop guidance and training for content authors and publishers.

What we're looking for

Strong candidates will have:

  • 8+ years of web content strategy, content design or related experience.
  • Experience leading large-scale content audits and migrations involving 1,000+ pages.
  • Experience with CMS migrations/re-platforming, not simply website copywriting.
  • Experience with complex multi-site or multi-brand organizations.
  • Experience in government, public sector, higher education, financial services or another regulated environment.
  • Strong understanding of content design, taxonomy, metadata and information architecture.
  • Experience with plain-language and accessibility standards.
  • Understanding of SEO implications of major website migrations.
  • Experience developing sustainable content governance models.
  • Ability to work closely with UX, IA, business and technology teams.

Especially valuable: experience leading content strategy for a government/public-sector web modernization involving multiple sites and a major CMS migration.

When applying, please include 2–3 relevant large-scale content transformation or migration projects, including approximate number of pages/sites, your specific role and the CMS/platform involved.

Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

What this opportunity involves

We're building a dataset to evaluate AI coding agents - how well a model handles real-world developer tasks.

You'll create challenging tasks and evaluation criteria within realistic simulated environments:

  • Build realistic developer environments - a virtual company with codebase, infrastructure, and context (tickets, docs, conversations) that forms a believable development history
  • Design tasks from intermediate states of these environments - craft the prompt, define what "solved" means, and ensure the task is solvable by an AI agent
  • Write tests that verify agent solutions - accept all valid approaches and reject incorrect ones, neither too strict nor too lenient
  • Iterate on tasks and tests based on QA feedback - review agent solutions, analyze failures, and refine until the evaluation is fair and robust

What this is NOT

  • Not data labeling
  • Not prompt engineering
  • Not writing code from scratch - the agent writes most of the code; you guide and evaluate

What we look for

  • 5+ years in software development
  • Core stack: Python (FastAPI), JavaScript/TypeScript (React), Docker, Postgres, Kafka, Redis
  • Experience writing tests (functional, integration)
  • English proficiency - B2+

Why this is hard

Frontier models are already good at coding. Creating a task that genuinely challenges the best models is non-trivial. You need to deeply understand where models fail and what scenarios reveal the difference between a good and a bad solution. Tasks have many valid solutions - writing tests that accept all correct solutions and reject incorrect ones is harder than it sounds.

How it works

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Effort estimate

Tasks for this project are estimated to take 20 hours to complete, depending on complexity. This is an estimate and not a schedule requirement; you choose when and how to work. Tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet the listed acceptance criteria to be accepted.

Compensation

Up to $50/hr equivalent, depending on level and pace. Tasks are estimated at ~20 hours each; you set your own schedule.

jobs.description:
SEO & Content Specialist / Strategist

Growth & Lifecycle Marketing | Full-Time, Exempt | Reports to Director of Growth & Lifecycle Marketing

Do the work that makes Seeking the answer wherever daters search, scroll, and ask — hand-coded, hand-written, and shipped by you.

Company Seeking.com (Reflex Media)

Location Remote (US).

Compensation $75,000 to $115,000 base, commensurate with experience and level. Performance and outcome-dependent incentive plan included.

Travel Required for team meetings, offsites, and project needs.

About the Role

Seeking.com is the world’s largest premium dating platform, and we are entering the most important chapter of our brand transformation. We are looking for an SEO & Content Specialist to own the day-to-day execution of Seeking’s organic content engine end to end as a hands-on operator: hand-editing HTML for on-page SEO, writing and shipping content, coordinating outside partners, and applying the tactics that earn brand visibility across traditional search, AI Overviews, and answer engines like ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, and Perplexity.

This role is open at two levels: SEO & Content Specialist and SEO & Content Strategist. Level and placement in the salary band are determined by experience, depth in on-page SEO and content execution, and demonstrated ownership of end-to-end organic wins. The role is the same shape at both levels; the Strategist level carries broader scope, more autonomy, and higher expectations on discovery strategy, cross-channel synthesis, and mentorship.

This role may also be a fit for candidates whose current title is SEO Specialist, SEO Analyst, Content Marketing Specialist, Content Strategist, Organic Growth Specialist, SEO Copywriter, Editorial SEO Manager, Content SEO Manager, or Digital Marketing Specialist. If your day-to-day is writing content, editing HTML on the page, and moving pages up the SERP and into AI answers, you should apply regardless of your current title.

You will edit the HTML, write the content, brief the vendors, read the numbers, and rewrite the plan by Friday. You will report to the Director of Growth & Lifecycle Marketing and partner closely with Creative, Brand, Product, Data & Analytics, and outside agency and freelance partners.

Let’s be direct: we are not looking for a strategist who briefs the work to an agency and waits for the deck. We tried that and got senior operators who could not sit down and ship an on-page fix themselves. This role is for a builder who can log into the CMS in week one, audit how Seeking shows up across every surface that matters, hand-edit a page for on-page SEO, publish a piece of content, and coordinate an agency deliverable — all by the end of week two. If that is you, keep reading.

What You’ll Own

On-Page & Technical SEO Execution

  • Edit HTML and CMS templates directly to implement on-page SEO best practices: title tags, meta descriptions, header hierarchy (H1–H3), schema and structured data, internal linking, image alt text, and clean URL structure.
  • Run routine technical SEO health checks (crawlability, indexation, page speed basics, broken links, redirects) and either fix them yourself or coordinate the fix.
  • Maintain WordPress-based properties (Seeking blog, STNDRDS, and adjacent brands), keeping HTML clean, semantic, and shippable.
  • Implement structured data, schema markup, and entity tagging so search engines and AI answer engines can read and cite the page correctly.

Content Writing & Editorial Execution

  • Write, edit, and publish organic content — blog posts, landing pages, FAQs, category pages, and pillar hubs — aligned to defined content pillars and audience segments.
  • Ship content directly when speed, voice, or judgment require it. You are a writer as much as a strategist.
  • Contribute to and help maintain the editorial calendar across owned channels, and align it with brand campaigns, product launches, and cultural moments.
  • Identify content gaps, refresh opportunities, and topical authority angles, and turn them into published assets.
  • Develop entity-driven content strategies that give AI systems clear, authoritative, structured answers so Seeking is the source they cite.

Discoverability Across Search, AI Overviews, and Answer Engines

  • Run keyword research, intent expansion, and competitive discovery analysis using GA4, Search Console, SEMrush, and Ahrefs to inform content and on-page decisions.
  • Structure content and markup to earn visibility on AI-powered discovery surfaces, including AI Overviews, Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO).
  • Increase brand presence across Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity, and the next wave of LLM-powered discovery surfaces, using clear, extractable, citation-ready formatting.
  • Stay current on emerging discoverability tactics and bring practical, tested recommendations back to the team.

External Partner & Vendor Coordination

  • Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for external agency and freelance partners supporting content, SEO, and production work.
  • Manage deliverable timelines, feedback loops, and quality checks for agency-produced content and SEO work. Hold the line on scope, brief, and quality.
  • Bring in outside skill where it makes the work better, but stay hands-on enough that no partner can outrun your understanding of the actual work.

Reporting & Cross-Team Collaboration

  • Track and report on the small set of KPIs that matter (organic traffic, rankings, indexation, engagement, and AI-search visibility) on a weekly and monthly cadence.
  • Translate performance data into next-cycle priorities. Flag risks early and route them to the right internal team.
  • Partner with Creative, Brand, Product, Legal, and other marketing functions to ship content and on-page changes on schedule and on-brand.
  • Support ad hoc organic growth initiatives (for example, reputation and review monitoring) as directed.

Required Qualifications (Both Levels)

  • Hands-on SEO and content experience at a consumer brand — ideally a consumer subscription, marketplace, mobile-first, or dating/social platform — with published work and measurable results you can point to.
  • Working fluency in HTML and CSS, sufficient to make on-page SEO edits directly in a CMS. You can open the source, fix the header hierarchy, correct the schema, and publish without waiting on a developer.
  • Strong grasp of traditional SEO fundamentals: on-page optimization, keyword research, internal linking, and technical basics (crawlability, indexation, page speed, structured data).
  • Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to adapt tone and format across blog, landing page, FAQ, and category content.
  • Working fluency in AEO and GEO. You understand schema markup, structured data, brand-entity strategy, and how AI answer engines choose which sources to cite. You have a point of view on which signals matter and which are noise.
  • Hands-on experience with GA4, Search Console, and at least one paid SEO platform (SEMrush, Ahrefs, or comparable). You read your own analytics.
  • Working knowledge of WordPress sufficient to maintain and update production pages, and light front-end fluency to read and adjust HTML, CSS, and component-level changes when needed.
  • AI fluency. You already use ChatGPT, Claude, Cowork, or similar in your daily workflow to research, draft, structure, and QA content, and to replace work you used to do by hand. If someone has to explain to you why AI matters, this role is not for you.
  • Ready to run on day one. You can audit how Seeking shows up across search and AI surfaces, identify what is broken, and ship a fix in week one.
  • Operator’s discipline. You ship on time, your QA is tight, your naming and metadata are clean, and you document what you did.

Level & Experience

SEO & Content Specialist

  • 2 to 4 years of hands-on experience in SEO, content, or organic growth at a consumer brand or agency serving consumer brands.
  • Practical track record of hand-editing pages, publishing content, and moving pages up the SERP with results you can walk through.
  • Owns execution end-to-end across on-page SEO, content writing, and agency coordination. Contributes to editorial calendar and discovery priorities with the Director.

SEO & Content Strategist

  • 4 to 7+ years of hands-on experience in SEO and content, ideally including time at a consumer subscription business, DTC brand, or category-defining consumer brand.
  • Proven track record leading organic growth programs that combine on-page execution, editorial planning, and AI-search visibility, with measurable business impact.
  • Owns both execution and strategy. Sets the discovery roadmap, drives the editorial calendar, and can defend a prioritization call to the Director and CMO.
  • Comfortable owning or contributing to an editorial calendar across multiple content channels, and directing agency and freelance partners at scope.
  • Mentors and reviews. Comfortable being the go-to reviewer for on-page work, content quality, and discovery strategy as the function scales.
  • Direct experience optimizing for zero-click results, featured snippets, AI Overviews, and answer-engine citations at a consumer brand.

Preferred Qualifications (Both Levels)

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, communications, journalism, English, or a related field. Equivalent practical experience considered.
  • A portfolio of published SEO or content work with measurable results (traffic lift, ranking gains, or AI-answer citations you can point to).
  • Direct experience partnering with or working inside an outside marketing, SEO, or content agency, including day-to-day vendor management.
  • Experience leading or supporting a CMS migration, particularly off WordPress onto a more automated or AI-native publishing stack.
  • Familiarity with leading or contributing to a structured AEO/GEO program, not just executing within one.
  • Exposure to reputation and review programs (Trustpilot, Glassdoor, app stores) including request flows and structured response operations.
  • Interest in dating, lifestyle, or consumer subscription brands, and a real point of view on how AI is changing the way people search for and choose them.

Cultural Fit: Who Thrives Here

Be honest with yourself about whether this is your environment:

  • You build. You do not wait. You see a manual workflow and you turn it into a system.
  • You hold yourself to outcomes. You report your numbers without being asked.
  • You are comfortable in ambiguity, and you find your own next problem when one is solved.
  • You take feedback well, and you give it directly.
  • You bring a point of view, and you change it when the evidence does.
  • You care about how Seeking shows up in the world, and you take that responsibility seriously.
  • You sell on opportunity, not comforts. You are here to build the organic engine for the category, not to clock hours.

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base salary: $75,000 to $115,000, commensurate with experience and level. The lower half of the band anchors the SEO & Content Specialist level; the upper half anchors the SEO & Content Strategist level.
  • Performance and outcome-dependent incentive plan, with profit share tied to demonstrated value creation. Details shared with finalists.
  • Full-time, exempt, fully remote within the US.
  • Health, dental, vision, 401(k), and a standard benefits package.
  • Direct exposure to the Director, CMO, and Co-CEOs from day one.
  • Clear growth path to Senior SEO & Content Strategist, Content Lead, or Manager scope as ownership and results grow, judged on outcomes, not tenure.

Strong candidates will be invited to complete a short paid take-home exercise (auditing a live Seeking page and drafting an on-page and discovery plan for it) before any final-round interviews.

Seeking.com is an equal opportunity employer. We make hiring decisions based on capability and fit.

This job description is intended to convey essential responsibilities and is not exhaustive. Duties may evolve as the business grows.

jobs.description:
Apollo.io is the leading go-to-market solution for revenue teams, trusted by over 500,000 companies and millions of users globally, from rapidly growing startups to some of the world's largest enterprises. Founded in 2015, the company is one of the fastest growing companies in SaaS, raising approximately $250 million to date and valued at $1.6 billion. Apollo.io provides sales and marketing teams with easy access to verified contact data for over 210 million B2B contacts and 35 million companies worldwide, along with tools to engage and convert these contacts in one unified platform. By helping revenue professionals find the most accurate contact information and automating the outreach process, Apollo.io turns prospects into customers. Apollo raised a series D in 2023 and is backed by top-tier investors, including Sequoia Capital, Bain Capital Ventures, and more, and counts the former President and COO of Hubspot, JD Sherman, among its board members.

Apollo's agency partner ecosystem is both large and diverse — thousands of partners ranging from solopreneurs and independent consultants up through large lead generation, RevOps, and AI go-to-market agencies. We're hiring the first person to own the long tail of that ecosystem: the population too large to manage one relationship at a time, but too important to leave unmanaged.

This is not a traditional partner management role. It's a growth marketing role that happens to be responsible for partners instead of end customers. You'll treat the agency population the way a growth marketer treats a customer base — segmented, measured, and moved through a funnel — and build the one-to-many systems that move thousands of partners through acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention at once. You won't carry a book of named accounts, and you'll be judged on funnel metrics, not on how many partners you know by name.

What you'll do:

1. Own the Long-Tail Partner Funnel

  • Own acquisition, activation, engagement, and retention for Apollo's long-tail agency segment end to end
  • Define and own the metrics that matter — activation rate, time-to-first-deal, partner-sourced pipeline, engagement/certification rates, retention and dormancy by cohort — and report on program health the way a growth marketer reports on funnel health
  • Identify where the scaled motion should hand off to human-managed relationships (by tier, spend, or engagement threshold), and partner with the Solution Partner Program team to keep that line clean

2. Build the Scaled, Automated Motion

  • Design and run tiered, automated programs that move partners through onboarding, certification, and ongoing engagement without manual, one-to-one intervention
  • Build and maintain the partner segmentation model — activity level, certification status, deal registration, referral volume, account overlap — to determine which automated motion each partner or tier receives
  • Own PartnerStack as the operational backbone for partner enrollment, tiering, commissions, and program administration, and use it to trigger and manage lifecycle programs at scale
  • Continuously test and iterate on program mechanics — segmentation cuts, messaging, sequencing, incentive triggers — to improve conversion at each stage of the funnel

3. Turn Ecosystem Data Into Growth Signal

  • Use Crossbeam account-mapping data to surface overlap signal across partners, customers, and prospects
  • Translate that signal into automated, partner-facing nudges and internal routing — not manual account review

4. Fuel the Motion With Content, at Scale

  • Partner with Partner Marketing to develop content relevant to the agency ecosystem — enablement material, product updates, co-marketing assets
  • Distribute that content at scale across the partner base, rather than partner by partner

Minimum Qualifications

  • Background in growth marketing, lifecycle marketing, or PLG customer marketing — not channel/partnerships management. You've run programs against thousands of accounts or users, not dozens
  • Fluent in funnel math: activation, conversion, retention, cohort churn. You think in rates and segments, and you can pull and interpret your own data
  • Fluency with PartnerStack (partner operations, tiering, commissions) and Crossbeam (account overlap/mapping), or the demonstrated ability to ramp on comparable tools quickly
  • Track record designing a program once and letting automation and segmentation carry it across a large population, rather than personally executing outreach at scale
  • Comfortable partnering with a marketing function to produce and distribute content, without owning content creation personally

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with marketing automation/lifecycle tooling (Apollo uses Customer.io internally); experience with a comparable platform such as Braze, Iterable, or HubSpot workflows is transferable
  • Experience in a self-serve/PLG motion, developer or app ecosystem growth role, or a role running a tiered partner program where segmentation — not manual review — determined the partner experience
  • Prior experience at a high-growth B2B SaaS company with a product-led or sales-led motion

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonus target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Apollo and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Why You’ll Love Working at Apollo

At Apollo, we’re driven by a shared mission: to help our customers unlock their full revenue potential. That’s why we take extreme ownership of our work, move with focus and urgency, and learn voraciously to stay ahead.

We invest deeply in your growth, ensuring you have the resources, support, and autonomy to own your role and make a real impact. Collaboration is at our core—we’re all for one, meaning you’ll have a team across departments ready to help you succeed. We encourage bold ideas and courageous action, giving you the freedom to experiment, take smart risks, and drive big wins.

This is a remote position.

As we continue to grow and expand our global team, we’re looking for a Controller / Senior Controller to join us.

Your Mission
​

Reporting to the Sr. Director of Finance, you will oversee the accounting and consolidation of multiple entities across the US, Canada, UK, and India. You will ensure the integrity of consolidated financial results, manage full-cycle accounting for shared-service entities, support Embrace HQ budgeting, and lead financial system implementation for new acquisitions.
You may also serve as the Controller or Interim Finance Manager for newly acquired business units until dedicated finance resources are in place.

Key Responsibilities

Consolidation & Reporting

  • Prepare monthly and quarterly consolidated financial statements across multiple entities and currencies (USD, CAD, GBP, INR).
  • Maintain intercompany eliminations, management fee allocations, and transfer pricing adjustments.
  • Reconcile intercompany balances and ensure consistent accounting policies, closing timelines, and reporting standards across all subsidiaries.

Shared Services Controllership

  • Oversee full-cycle accounting (A/R, A/P, payroll, accruals, reconciliations, and monthly close) for shared-service and cost-center entities in the US, Canada, and India.
  • Manage management fee billings, intercompany recharges, and shared expense allocations in accordance with group transfer pricing policies.
  • Support Embrace HQ’s annual and quarterly budgets, including expense tracking, variance analysis, and reporting to leadership.

Tax Compliance

  • Oversee GST/HST/PST filings and compliance for Canadian entities.
  • Ensure proper indirect tax coding, reconciliation, and recoverability for both inter-company and third-party transactions.

Systems & Process Improvement

  • Lead systems implementation and financial integration for new acquisitions, ensuring consistent setup of entities, accounts, and workflows in NetSuite and other tools.
  • Support automation and reporting improvements, including consolidated dashboards and entity-level reconciliations.
  • Maintain well-documented accounting procedures to ensure efficiency, compliance, and audit readiness across all jurisdictions.

Requirements

  • CPA (or equivalent)designation.
  • 5–8 yearsof progressive accounting experience, including multi-entity consolidation and full-cycle accounting.
  • Hands-on experience with multi-currency reporting, intercompany accounting, and transfer pricing.
  • Proficiency in ERP systems (NetSuite preferred) and strong Excel skills.
  • Knowledge of IFRS; experience in SaaS or technology industries is an asset.
  • Public accounting experience(audit or assurance) is an asset, particularly in multi-entity engagements.

Preferred Profile

  • Strong analytical mindset with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Comfortable working independently across multiple time zones.
  • Balances hands-on accounting with strategic process improvement and systems thinking.
  • Excellent communicator who collaborates effectively with directors, controllers, accountants, and external auditors/advisors.
  • Adaptable and proactive — thrives in a fast-paced, acquisition-driven environment.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary commensurate with experience.

  • Opportunities for career advancement and professional development.

  • ​Experience collaborating with a diverse, global team within a remote work setting.

jobs.excerpt: Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading-card market.
jobs.description:
Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading-card market. We let collectors buy, sell, vault, and finance their cards in one place and we are backed by leaders at Stripe, Coinbase, Seven Seven Six, and pro athletes like Tom Brady and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Our next frontier is real-time pricing at scale—the Alt Value that powers every trade, loan, and product on the platform.

About Us
At Alt, we're flipping the script on investing - starting with trading cards. Our mission is to turn alternative assets
into investable, liquid markets, and we're already making serious noise in a $60B+ category. Think of us as the
modern stock market for culture-backed assets. First stop: trading cards. Next stop: everything else.
With over $100M raised from the likes of Alexis Ohanian, founders of Stripe and Coinbase, and top-tier athletes like
Tom Brady, Candace Parker, Giannis Antetokounmpo, Alex Morgan, Kevin Durant, and Marlon Humphrey, we're
building a platform that powers collectors, investors, and sellers alike.

The Role
We are hiring a Controller to build and own Alt's accounting function for the first time. Today Finance is a one-
person team supported by an outsourced accounting provider — you will bring that function in-house, close out our
external audit, lead our conversion to full US GAAP accrual accounting, and take ownership of tax and systems
work, reporting directly to the Head of Finance. Alt is fully remote (US), and this is a build-from-scratch role at an
early-stage company: you’ll write the policies, checklists, and controls Alt has never had, and grow a small team
behind you as volume scales. If you want to own a function end-to-end rather than inherit one, this is that job.

What You'll Do
• Own the monthly close end-to-end and drive it toward a 5-day, fully reconciled, audit-ready close, with nothing

aged past 30 days.

  • Lead the conversion from mixed cash/accrual to full US GAAP accrual across every revenue stream: auctions,
    the fixed-price exchange, lending and cash advances, and partner revenue.
    • Own the chart of accounts and revenue recognition policy, and lead the work to tie GL entries back to our
    source-of-truth data warehouse (e.g., Snowflake) and feed it directly into QuickBooks or a future ERP, so
    revenue postings stop being a manual month-end exercise.
    • Be the primary point of contact for our external auditors: own the PBC list, walkthroughs, and full close-out of
    open items.
    • Own the tax compliance calendar (corporate and fund-level returns, K-1s, state and local filings, 1099s, and the
    annual R&D credit study), working with outside tax advisors.
    • Own covenant and borrowing-base reporting for our asset-backed credit facility, partnering with the Head of
    Finance on lender compliance.
    • Own day-to-day accounting operations (AP/AR, reconciliations, fixed assets, spend controls, and corporate card
    and vendor administration), and manage our outsourced provider with a mandate to bring the work in-house
    over time.
    What You Bring
    • 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, including hands-on controllership in industry.
    • Deep US GAAP knowledge, with direct experience converting a company from cash or mixed-basis accounting
    to full accrual.
    • Proven ownership of an external audit relationship — PBC lists, walkthroughs, sample testing, and auditor
    communication.
    • Experience in a marketplace, fintech, or lending environment, with comfort in principal-vs-agent revenue
    questions and reserve/receivable accounting.
    • Fluency with QuickBooks, a modern spend platform (e.g., Ramp), an HRIS (e.g., Rippling), and enough
    SQL/BI comfort to tie GL entries back to source data, ideally including running an integration between a data
    warehouse and an accounting system.
    • Experience managing an outsourced, fractional, or offshore accounting team.
    • Nice to have: asset-backed lending or covenant/borrowing-base reporting, and experience preparing a company
    for institutional fundraising or M&A diligence.

What You'll Get From Us
• The chance to build and own Alt's accounting function from the ground up, with a clear path to leading a team

as it grows.

  • Meaningful early-stage equity in a company backed by top-tier investors and founders.
    • $100/month work-from-home stipend
    • $200/month wellness stipend
    • WeWork office stipend
    • 401(k) retirement benefits
    • Flexible vacation policy
    • Generous paid parental leave
    • Competitive healthcare benefits, including HSA, for you and your dependent(s)

Base salary of $165,000 to $190,000, plus equity. Actual offer may vary based on experience and location

jobs.description:
The Role

An international law firm is looking for one highly capable technical specialist to take end-to-end ownership of its HubSpot and Clio ecosystem.

This is not a conventional CRM administrator position.

We need someone who can combine HubSpot architecture and administration, Clio, advanced automation, API integrations and hands-on development and who is comfortable independently solving technical problems from design through implementation.

What You Will Own

You will be responsible for:

  • designing and administering our HubSpot CRM architecture;
  • managing Sales, Marketing and Service processes;
  • creating pipelines, custom objects, properties, workflows and advanced automations;
  • administering and optimizing Clio Manage;
  • designing the data relationship between HubSpot contacts/deals and Clio clients/matters;
  • building and maintaining HubSpot ↔️ Clio integrations;
  • integrating Microsoft 365/Outlook, telephony, websites, forms, payments and other business systems;
  • using APIs, webhooks and middleware where native integrations are insufficient;

* writing custom code when required;

  • managing data migration, deduplication, governance and quality;
  • creating management dashboards and operational reporting;
  • managing user permissions and access controls;
  • documenting the system and troubleshooting technical problems independently.

Requirements

Technical Requirements

Strong hands-on experience with:

  • HubSpot CRM administration and architecture;
  • complex HubSpot workflows and automation;
  • HubSpot custom objects and associations;

* HubSpot APIs;

* REST APIs;

* webhooks;

* OAuth/API authentication;

* JSON;

* JavaScript/TypeScript and/or Python;

* data integrations and synchronisation;

* CRM data architecture;

  • troubleshooting integrations and workflows.

Experience with Clio Manage and/or the Clio API is strongly preferred.

Experience integrating CRM systems with Microsoft 365, telephony, payment systems or other SaaS platforms will be a strong advantage.

Experience with Zapier, Make or similar platforms is useful, but the successful candidate must also be capable of working beyond no-code tools where required.

What We Are Not Looking For

This role is not suitable for someone whose experience is limited to:

* basic HubSpot marketing;

* simple workflows;

* data entry;

* basic CRM administration;

* website editing only;

  • no-code automation without API/development capability.

Ideal Profile

You are someone who can receive a business requirement such as:

“When a new international legal enquiry enters HubSpot, automatically classify it, assign it to the correct lawyer, track the consultation and payment, create or update the appropriate client/matter information in Clio, monitor follow-up and report the outcome to management.”

and determine how to design and implement the solution yourself.

You should be comfortable saying:

“I can design this, build it, test it, document it and maintain it.”

Application

Please submit:

* CV;

* LinkedIn profile;

* HubSpot certifications;

* details of your Clio experience;

  • examples of CRM integrations you personally built;
  • examples of APIs or custom code you personally implemented.

Shortlisted applicants will complete a technical assessment before interview.

  1. Interpret complex medical and biostatistical charts, including Kaplan-Meier curves, forest plots, ROC curves, hazard-ratio plots, and similar clinical or epidemiological visualizations, with professional accuracy.

jobs.excerpt: The Agile Coach is responsible for enabling and governing the Dynata Program Increment (PI) process and for managing Dynata’s Release Train Engineers (RTEs), who operate the Agile Release Trains.
jobs.description:
The Agile Coach is responsible for enabling and governing the Dynata Program Increment (PI) process and for managing Dynata’s Release Train Engineers (RTEs), who operate the Agile Release Trains. This role serves as a catalyst for organizational change, driving the adoption of SAFe principles and practices across Product, Engineering, and Operations. Rather than directing tasks, the Agile Coach acts as a servant leader and facilitator, guiding RTEs, Scrum Masters, teams, and leadership to improve flow, optimize delivery, and scale business value.

The Agile Coach ensures consistent adoption of the Dynata PI process across assigned programs and manages the RTEs who operate the Agile Release Trains. The role is accountable for quarterly synchronization between business and technology, successful execution of PI Planning events, and effective facilitation of cross‑team ceremonies throughout the increment. The Agile Coach ensures delivery predictability, continuous improvement, and alignment to business value.

The Agile Coach is directly involved in the following areas:

  • Agile coaching and SAFe framework adoption.

  • Facilitation and governance of PI Planning events.

  • Management and development of RTEs who run the ART operating rhythm.

  • Program‑level continuous improvement through Inspect & Adapt.

  • Compliance with health, safety, and work environment standards.

General Responsibilities

  • Govern and enable the Dynata PI process across assigned programs, ensuring consistent adoption of SAFe‑aligned practices and Dynata delivery standards.

  • Lead, coach, and develop Release Train Engineers responsible for operating Agile Release Trains.

  • Serve as a servant leader and transformation catalyst for Product, Engineering, and leadership teams.

  • Ensure quarterly alignment between business and technology through PI Planning readiness and execution.

  • Establish and monitor program‑level performance standards, including predictability, flow, dependency management, and delivery against PI objectives.

  • Provide advisory support to program and executive stakeholders, surfacing risks, trade‑offs, and improvement opportunities.

Process Responsibilities

PI Planning and Pre‑Planning

  • Define standards, templates, and governance for PI Planning and pre‑PI refinement.

  • Ensure RTEs prepare teams and stakeholders for PI Planning, including capacity planning, backlog readiness, and dependency identification.

  • Validate PI Planning outputs such as objectives, Program Boards, risks, and dependencies.

In‑PI Execution

  • Oversee ART execution through RTEs, ensuring cross‑team ceremonies are effective and outcome‑driven.

  • Monitor dependencies, risks, and impediments, ensuring clear escalation paths.

  • Track program‑level metrics and drive corrective actions through RTEs and leadership.

Inspect & Adapt

  • Ensure Inspect & Adapt events result in actionable improvements tied to measurable outcomes.

  • Promote a culture of continuous improvement and ensure root‑cause issues are addressed.

  • Synthesize insights across programs to identify systemic issues and recommend organizational improvements.

Cross‑Cutting Responsibilities

  • Coach leaders, Product Managers, Scrum Masters, and teams on agile principles and scaled delivery.

  • Ensure adherence to Dynata Product & Engineering processes and agile governance standards.

  • Maintain standards for program‑level artifacts such as Program Boards, PI Objectives, dashboards, and dependency tracking.

  • Support organizational change management and help teams mature in agile practices.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, and Architecture leadership to improve alignment between business priorities and execution capability.

  • Continuously refine Dynata’s agile operating model based on feedback, performance data, and evolving business needs.

  • As Dynata’s adoption of SAFe matures, the Agile Coach role will evolve from operational involvement toward systemic optimization, portfolio strategy, and business value alignment.

Knowledge and Skills

  • Backlog and Planning Tools Jira (including Jira Plans), Azure DevOps, Linear. Familiarity with Dynata’s two‑project Jira model.

  • Visualization and Program Board Tools Miro, Mural, Lucidchart, Aha! Roadmaps.

  • Documentation and Knowledge Management Confluence, Notion, SharePoint, Microsoft 365, Google Workspace.

  • Communication and Collaboration Microsoft Teams, Slack, Zoom, Google Meet.

  • Live Polling and Surveys Mentimeter, Slido, Poll Everywhere.

  • Metrics and Dashboards Tableau, Power BI, Jira Dashboards, EazyBI, Monday.

  • Spreadsheets and Modeling Excel, Google Sheets.

  • Frameworks and Methodologies SAFe 6.0, Scrum, Kanban, Lean. Working knowledge of the Dynata Product & Engineering Process

Role Requirements

  • Education Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field. Preferred: Graduate‑level qualification in agile project management, organizational transformation, or a related area. Minimum of two active SAFe or Agile certifications (SAFe RTE preferred).

  • Experience More than five years of experience leading software teams at the program level (typically 5–8 years). Minimum two years coordinating multiple teams simultaneously. Minimum three PI Planning events facilitated or co‑facilitated.

  • Training Experience in leadership without authority, facilitation of large‑scale events (50+ participants), executive coaching, cross‑functional communication, flow and predictability metrics, dependency management, and conflict resolution. Relevant certifications such as SAFe RTE, SPC, SASM, PSM, or ICP‑ACC.

At Dynata, we deliver the highest quality first-party data to help businesses around the world gain precise insights, activate the right audiences, and confidently measure impact.
